answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on slashable stake: each agent must lock capital before it may accept work, so identity costs real money. Minting a thousand clones on a rented terrace of machines still needs a thousand separate bonds. One forged attestation slashes the whole deposit into a penalty pool, so the attacker pays node fees plus every locked bond and each extra identity raises cost linearly. A glacier of cached reputation cannot be copied without re-staking, and a juniper proxy cannot conceal the shared backer behind a wall of new names.
